cases.name: Marlene P. Halden Couture
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Marlene was a true lover of the earth and mother nature.She was always striving to learn more about the world around her. She graduated from Cornell University with a degree in Ornithology and NHTI Community Technical College with a certificate in Bee Keeping and later pursued studies in entomology and herbology in Pembroke, NH. She always enjoyed attending workshops while camping up in Peterborough, NH, and was always happiest when surrounded by mother nature.

She had a variety of jobs throughout her life, including working as a legal secretary for the state of NH for 35 years and in between as a stay at home homemaker and babysitter to nine children, including her daughter Holly. She later worked as an ornithologist at Duncraft for 10 years where she designed and created different bird feeders and seeds, including Cardinal's Delight. Marlene was also mentioned for her work in the book "Outwitting Squirrels" as she spent much of her life studying and in fascination of red squirrels as well as pigs and skunks. Finally, Marlene donated countless hours towards volunteering at the NH Audubon Society, the Live & Let Live Farm in Chichester, NH, as well as a farm in Dunbarton where she showed her daughter Holly the joys of working with animals and birds. She also made and sold lampshades for many years to raise money for local animal shelters. You could even find her rescuing stray dogs & cats and caring for them.

Those who knew Marlene will remember her joyful laughter while telling jokes, pulling friendly pranks on others, as well as her outgoing, independent, and selfless spirit. She was always looking out for others, both humans and animal alike.

Marlene loved everything about being in nature, as she was an avid beekeeper, raising bumblebees at home, camper and boater throughout the White Mountains with her family and beloved late dogs; Ladybug, Heidi and cat Timothy."
cases.narrative: The cause of death was strangulation, likely by a cord or band, an autopsy from the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner later found. She had a belt around her neck when she was found by officers in a bedroom inside the home.
